correctness.rationale: The diagonal normal operator gives closed numerical range equal to the closed convex hull of {n^{-σ-it}}∪{0}. The logarithmic spiral has maximal positive imaginary support m_a=e^{-a(π+arctan(1/a))}/sqrt(1+a²), a=σ/t; this upper bounds any centered disk. The actual integer eigenvalues at ceiling exp((π/2)/t) and ceiling exp((π+arctan(1/a))/t), plus 1, form a zero-containing triangle with all side-line distances ≥m_a(1−o(1)); the other two distances are asymptotically larger. Ceiling logarithmic errors are exponentially tiny. Thus r∼m_a and the limit constant is e^{-1}, while two negative-real conjugate-phase eigenvalues plus 1 prove positive inradius for any t≠0.
